title: SRM: sparse segment reservation mapper and telemetry-driven compaction plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: As models run longer sequences with continuous batching, KV cache fragmentation grows due to variable-sized KV entries across model families and mixed-latency request patterns. Fragmentation increases peak GPU memory usage, reduces effective cache hit rate, and forces evictions that regress latency and quality for tail requests.

Goal: Design and implement a Sparse Segment Reservation Mapper (SRM) and a telemetry-driven compaction/eviction policy that reduces long-tail fragmentation without regressing throughput. The SRM should: (1) allow small contiguous reservations for transient KV entries, (2) enable low-cost background compaction when GPU utilization windows allow, and (3) expose signals for autoscaler and routing to prefer low-fragment workloads.

Scope: allocator metadata, reservation paths, compaction tickets, eviction scoring, telemetry hooks, and unit+integration tests. Does NOT include a full replacement of the runtime allocator or changes to cross-node sharding logic (future follow-ups).

Why this is different: Rather than coarse slab/buddy approaches, SRM keeps a lightweight sparse mapping layer that tracks segment occupancy at a sub-page granularity and orchestrates epochal compaction using "compaction tickets" that schedule relocations only when GPU SM utilization < threshold. The approach targets reduced copy amplification and prioritizes inexpensive local defrag before global relocates.

Success metrics:
- 25% reduction in 95th-percentile GPU resident KV memory for mixed workloads (chat + embedding/rerank).
- <5% throughput regression during normal traffic.
- 10% absolute improvement in tail hit-rate for long-lived chat sessions.

Artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwoodai.internal/display/RUNTIME/SRM+design, perf dashboard: https://grafana.redwoodai.internal/d/kv-frag/srm-experiments, prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1439
updates: 2026-02-28: Ticket created. Initial problem framing after postmortem of perf regression on 2026-02-22 incident. Assigned to Liam. Linked to runtime-memory-2026 initiative.

2026-03-02: Spike complete: implemented in-proc SRM prototype in the memory playground. Observed 18% p95 resident reduction for synthetic homogeneous streams; mixed streams showed 9% reduction. Notes in draft design doc.

2026-03-04: Design review with Core Runtime and Observability teams. Action items: add compaction ticket backpressure, define telemetry schema, and ensure compaction works with continuous-batching pipeline to avoid KV race conditions.

2026-03-07: Implemented compaction ticket queue with priority tiers (low/medium/high) and a token bucket gated by GPU idle estimator. Ran microbenchmarks showing <3% throughput impact when token bucket full; otherwise defers compaction.

2026-03-10: Integration test flake found where compaction moved an entry still being read by streaming response; added ephemeral pinning to reservations and strengthened KV read-after-move validation. Test added to CI.
2026-03-10: Updated perf dashboard links and opened prototype PR for internal review (runtime PR #1439).
tasks: Finalize SRM metadata layout and in-memory representation (compact, atomic ops)
Implement compaction ticket scheduler with GPU-utilization gating
Add eviction scorer that uses SRM density + request-age + model-affinity
Instrument telemetry (per-request KV fragmentation events, compaction time, bytes moved)
Write unit tests for reservation allocation, pin/unpin semantics, and race conditions
Add integration test in continuous-batching harness and run against mixed workloads
Performance run on dedicated infra; export dashboard and compare baseline
Rollout plan: staged flag behind runtime-1.26, enable on low-traffic region, monitor SLOs
acceptance_criteria: P95 GPU resident KV memory reduced >= 20% on 3 representative mixed workloads compared to baseline
End-to-end latency regression <= 5% at target QPS during steady-state
No correctness regressions: no duplicate KV reads, no lost/overwritten entries under streaming concurrency
Telemetry emitted for every compaction ticket and eviction decision with trace correlation
Feature guarded by runtime flag and rollout steps documented
